summary:
Drupa 2028 has attracted exhibitor registrations from 38 countries, signalling strong global interest in the print and packaging fair.
Taking place in Düsseldorf on May 9–17, 2028, it will emphasise automation, AI, robotics and circularity through integrated production solutions.
Exhibitor registration closes on October 31, 2026, with details of new formats and programming due in early 2027.

title: Performance Days Munich draws 5,170 visitors at largest edition
summary:
Performance Days Munich recorded its largest edition, welcoming 5,170 trade visitors, around 20 per cent more than last autumn, and 599 exhibitors across 27,500 sq m.
New forums covered cellulose, garment technology, digital design and sustainability, while a repair service demonstrated circularity.
The next edition, on March 17–18, 2027, will explore bio-based dyeing, finishing and processing.

title: Sunrise’s MAD 2.29 bn Investment: A turning point for Textile exports?
summary:
Shengtai’s Morocco textile-park plan has Chinese outbound-investment clearance and targets up to MAD 2.3 billion in Fez and Skhirat.
Planned annual capacity includes 100,000 spindles, 10,800 tonnes of dyed fabric, 15 million metres of woven fabric and 22 million garments.
Fez broke ground in December 2025, but commercial output and Skhirat status were unconfirmed by October 14, 2026.

title: India, US ‘pretty close’ to trade deal: Trump
summary:
US President Trump said India and the US were close to finalising a bilateral trade agreement, describing it as different from previous deals. 
His remarks came as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is visiting India to discuss trade, energy, technology and defence. 
Rubio said only a few issues remained unresolved and expressed confidence that the pact would be finalised shortly.

title: ICE cotton extends gains as weak dollar, firm crude lend support
summary:
ICE cotton December 2026 futures settled at 80.88 cents per pound, up 0.94 per cent, as a weaker US dollar and stronger crude oil supported export competitiveness and cotton's edge over synthetics.
Gains were capped by expectations of an accelerated US harvest, with USDA reporting 41 per cent picked, ahead of the five-year average.
Volume rose 14 per cent, but trade stayed subdued.

title: Qantara West's $1.54 bn pipeline: Can Egypt expand its textile reach?
summary:
Egypt is expanding Qantara West capacity beyond cut-and-sew, adding spinning, weaving, dyeing and garment production closer to European markets.
Jasan Group has broken ground on a $117 million complex targeting 90 per cent exports and about 6,000 direct jobs.
SCZONE reports 54 Qantara West projects worth about $1.54 billion; apparel exports rose 16 per cent in January-August 2026.

title: EU-Mercosur pact opens an early window for European textile exports
summary:
EURATEX, ABIT and FITA launched an EU–Mercosur textile and apparel dialogue in Fortaleza, Brazil, to advance market access and resilient value chains.
The interim pact has applied provisionally since May 1, 2026; Mercosur’s 35 per cent textile duty will fall to zero over eight years.
EU–Mercosur textile and clothing trade was nearly €700 million (~$787 million) in 2025, including €495 million EU exports.

title: India-New Zealand FTA takes effect, opens duty-free textile access
summary:
India-New Zealand FTA took effect on October 20, opening duty-free access in New Zealand for Indian textiles, apparel, leather and footwear. 
New Zealand removed duties on all Indian export tariff lines, including peak tariffs of up to 10 per cent; faster customs are expected to lower landed costs. 
The pact backs a 2030 goal to double goods and services trade to NZ$7 billion ($3.99 billion).

title: Dornbirn GFC 2027 to run September 14–16 in Austria
summary:
The 66th Dornbirn GFC will run from September 14–16, 2027, in Austria, starting a day earlier than usual to help visitors combine it with ITMA in Hanover.
Five themes will cover fibre innovation, circularity, nonwovens, processing and protective clothing.
The call for papers opens in mid-November 2026, while ticket sales begin in late March 2027. Early hotel bookings are encouraged.

title: How leading footwear brands are winning with comfort tech
summary:
Global footwear brands are designing around cushioning, lighter construction and all-day ease as shoppers put comfort ahead of sharp silhouettes.
Analyst David Swartz says consumers will pay more for comfort, with Skechers, Birkenstock, On, Hoka, Adidas, Nike and Crocs gaining.
Running foams, 3D printing and athleisure are pushing sneakers and sandals into daily wear as formal footwear weakens.

title: New Zealand's apparel imports rise 5.9% in September 2026
summary:
New Zealand's apparel imports rose 5.9 per cent year on year to NZ$190.20 million ($107.85 million) in September, a third straight monthly gain.
January–September imports were virtually flat at NZ$1.567 billion, with knitted apparel up 0.7 per cent and non-knitted down 0.8 per cent.
Exports fell 2.6 per cent to NZ$18.52 million in September, as knitted apparel shipments dropped but non-knitted exports rose.

title: Luxury’s split market: Ultra-rich spend, aspirational buyers retreat
summary:
Global luxury fashion revenue fell 0.5 per cent in 2025 and is forecast to grow 2.2 per cent in 2026, with growth tapering towards 2031 as aspirational buyers curb spending.
LVMH led luxury goods in 2025 with a 21 per cent share; fashion held 29 per cent, behind watches and jewellery at 34 per cent.
US 2026 revenue is estimated at $96.9 billion, ahead of China at $92.7 billion.

title: Bangladesh's apparel exports to EU may gain in late 2026: Eurostat
summary:
Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the EU could regain momentum late in 2026 and in 2027 as the bloc’s import decline narrows, according to the Eurostat data. 
EU apparel imports fell 3.83 per cent to €60.29 billion (~$67.74 billion) in January-August; Bangladesh’s shipments dropped 11.67 per cent to €11.93 billion (~$13.40 billion). 
August EU import value rose 0.72 per cent year on year.

title: France's Damartex protects profitability amid Q1 revenue decline
summary:
French apparel group Damartex reported an 8 per cent revenue decline to €98.6 million (~$110.68 million) in Q1 FY27 amid hot weather and weak consumer confidence. 
Fashion sales fell as seasonal purchases were delayed, while home and healthcare businesses also declined. 
The group prioritised profitability and operational discipline without disclosing quarterly profit or margin figures.

title: India’s athleisure trend is growing, but sportswear is just 1%
summary:
India’s apparel market is valued at $95.7 billion in 2025, but sportswear holds only about 1 per cent despite athleisure hype and growth expectations.
CMAI-1Lattice data shows men lead sportswear at $630 million, ahead of kids at $250 million and women at $150 million.
Among men, 17 per cent of track pant or suit buyers bought online, while major offline chains already stock the category.

title: Hong Kong’s T-shirt imports defy wider apparel decline
summary:
Hong Kong’s apparel imports fell 4.58 per cent YoY to $3.976 billion in January–August 2026, but T-shirts rose 3.10 per cent to become the largest imported apparel category.
Jerseys slipped to second, while trousers and shorts fell 8.23 per cent and shirts dropped 11.29 per cent, according to TexPro.
Home textile imports rose 7.91 per cent to $179.265 million, led by bed textiles.

title: Vietnam’s export growth masks margin crunch?
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and garment exports hit nearly $31.7 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up 2.9 per cent year on year, but profitability remains squeezed.
Smaller batches, tighter deadlines and buyer delays are weakening scale economies and order visibility.
Logistics costs of 9–10 per cent of export-import value, congestion and surcharges make delivery efficiency crucial.

title: UK’s garment exports dip 10% in August 2026
summary:
United Kingdom clothing exports fell 10.1 per cent year on year to £214 million (~$282 million) in August 2026, ONS data showed, easing from £235 million in July.
Textile fabric exports dropped 10.41 per cent to £172 million, while fibre exports rose year on year to £39 million but fell from July.
In Q2 2026, clothing exports slipped 1.93 per cent to £711 million, with 2025 exports down 9.17 per cent.

title: UK’s clothing imports down 10% in Aug 2026
summary:
UK clothing imports fell 10.37 per cent YoY to £1.494 billion (~$1.966 billion) in August 2026 but rose 4.76 per cent from July.
Fabric imports dropped 4.33 per cent YoY and 18.79 per cent monthly to £419 million; fibre imports stood at £22 million.
Q2 2026 clothing imports fell 3.67 per cent, while full-year 2025 imports rose 6.05 per cent.

title: EU traceability push puts Bangladesh’s SMEs to the test
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment SMEs could face a disproportionate burden from EU traceability and DPP rules as they invest in data collection, verification, system integration and training.
Stakeholders seek clearer rules, coordinated data systems, targeted financing and enough preparation time to prevent smaller suppliers bearing excessive compliance costs.
